cards.claim_text_bounded: ItemCF estimates item-item similarity from historical interaction overlap and aggregates neighbor evidence, whereas BPR supplies a pairwise implicit-feedback objective that can train matrix factorization or another differentiable scorer.
cards.support_scope: Architecture and objective definitions only; the sources use different historical evaluation settings and provide no dataset-v5 result.
forbidden_extrapolations: Neither source establishes a ranking on dataset v5.
Unobserved interactions are not automatically true negative preferences.
counter_evidence: BPR performance changes with negative sampling and optimization choices; ItemCF changes with similarity, normalization, and neighborhood rules.

cards.claim_text_bounded: NCF learns nonlinear interaction functions from user/item IDs, while DeepFM jointly models low- and high-order interactions over sparse feature fields for CTR prediction; their input and task contracts are therefore not interchangeable.
cards.support_scope: Source-defined inputs and objectives; no claim about their relative v5 performance.
forbidden_extrapolations: CTR AUC/log-loss does not establish full-catalog top-k performance.
Source-native sampled leave-one-out results do not establish a v5 ranking.
counter_evidence: DeepFM needs feature fields that an interaction-only v5 comparator may not have; NCF ID embeddings do not define zero-edge item representations.

cards.claim_text_bounded: In the inspected industrial references, candidate generation or matching reduces a very large corpus to a smaller set, after which a richer ranking stage can score hundreds of items; a two-tower model must therefore be labeled by its retrieval, pre-ranking, or ranking role.
cards.support_scope: System-stage definitions and matching constraints in the cited systems; dataset v5 has no frozen two-stage contract yet.

locator.anchor: Sections 2 System Overview, 3 Candidate Generation, and 4 Ranking

forbidden_extrapolations: Retrieval-stage recall does not prove ranking-stage quality.
Do not assume dataset v5 requires this topology before Stage 1E freezes the architecture contract.
No cited paper establishes a v5 architecture ranking.
counter_evidence: Pair-agnostic independent towers limit target-specific interaction; ContextGNN and T2Diff are controls for that limitation.

cards.claim_text_bounded: Wide & Deep combines a linear component over explicit cross-product features for memorization with an embedding/MLP component for generalization and trains them jointly for its reported ranking task.
cards.support_scope: Only the source-defined memorization/generalization distinction and joint model; no Apriori component is evaluated.

locator.anchor: Sections 3.1 Wide Component, 3.2 Deep Component, and 3.3 Joint Training

forbidden_extrapolations: Wide & Deep does not prove that an Apriori branch is effective.
The production result does not establish a v5 architecture ranking.
counter_evidence: The wide component depends on manually specified cross-product features and leakage-safe feature construction.

cards.claim_text_bounded: LightGCN and the retained graph-contrastive controls learn from an observed user-item graph and trainable ID embeddings; improvements on sparse observed graphs cannot establish recommendation capability for an item with zero training edges.
cards.support_scope: Observed-graph inputs and propagation/contrastive mechanisms; this is a boundary on what the sources can support.
forbidden_extrapolations: Sparse-edge graph improvement does not prove zero-edge cold-item capability.
No source establishes a v5 architecture ranking.
counter_evidence: Zero-edge items require a separately specified feature, content, or inductive path; none is defined by vanilla LightGCN.

cards.claim_text_bounded: Encoder complexity and training objective must be controlled separately: BPR specifies pairwise ranking, sampled two-tower training introduces negative-distribution effects, and DirectAU directly optimizes alignment and uniformity.
cards.support_scope: Objective and sampling mechanisms only; relative v5 effects remain an empirical benchmark question.

locator.anchor: Sections 3 and 4 on alignment, uniformity, and direct optimization

forbidden_extrapolations: Do not attribute a source-native gain solely to architecture when objectives or sampling differ.
Do not infer a v5 ranking.
counter_evidence: A simpler encoder with a different objective can outperform a deeper encoder under a source-native protocol; only a factorial or harmonized benchmark isolates the contribution.

cards.claim_text_bounded: ContextGNN and T2Diff are recent controls for the pair-agnostic two-tower boundary: the former introduces pair-aware local graph context with an exploratory fallback, while the latter introduces training-time cross-interaction for efficient matching.
cards.support_scope: Mechanism and stage-role evidence from final 2025 records; neither source has been run on v5.

locator.anchor: Abstract and Method sections on pair-wise context and two-tower fallback

forbidden_extrapolations: Do not claim either control outranks another architecture on v5.
Matching-stage evidence is not ranking-stage evidence.
Observed local graph context is not zero-edge cold-item evidence.
counter_evidence: Both controls add assumptions and computation; their transport depends on the final v5 stage topology and inputs.

cards.claim_text_bounded: A dataset-v5 architecture comparison must harmonize split, candidate universe, stage role, input features, objective, negative sampling, tuning budget, and evaluator; the inspected architecture papers alone cannot supply a v5 ranking.
cards.support_scope: Planning constraint derived from incompatible source-native tasks/protocols and the locked Stage 1A methodology; it is not a benchmark result.
